blocks.text: The risk score ranges from 0 to 1. It is the estimated chance that the province's hunger-and-food-price score -- regional hunger from the SWS survey plus twice the gap between the province's food inflation and the five-province average -- is above its usual level, the median of the past published quarters. A higher score means this combined pressure is more likely to be above its usual level. It is not a measure of how many families lack food. This report uses three risk levels: Alert (0.60 and above), High (0.50 to below 0.60) and Not elevated (below 0.50).

items: In 2026 Q4, the risk score for Quezon is 0.92, which is at the Alert level.
Food prices are the main factor behind the score, accounting for about 67% of the factors, and they raise the risk.
Compared with 2026 Q3, the risk score increased by 0.03 (from 0.89 to 0.92).
The 2026 Q4 value is a forecast issued 2026-10-01; its outcome is not yet known.

blocks.note: Risk levels: Alert is 0.60 and above, High is 0.50 to below 0.60, and Not elevated is below 0.50. The main factor is the largest of the five factors behind each score. 2026 Q4: forecast, lead 1, issued 2026-10-01.

blocks.text: As shown in Figure 1, food prices account for about 67% of the factors behind Quezon's risk score in 2026 Q4 and raise the risk. Jobs and employment account for about 18% and also raise the risk. Fish kills account for about 12% and lower the risk. Remittances from OFWs account for about 2% and lower the risk. Weather and climate account for about 1% and lower the risk. Compared with 2026 Q3, the share of food prices rose from 27% to 67%. Of everything behind Quezon's score, about 26% comes from the regional hunger survey and the last published result, about 6% from the tone of the news and news reports that match none of the five factors, and about 68% from the five factors shown in the figure.

blocks.label: Figure 1
blocks.title: Factors Behind the Risk Score in Quezon, 2026 Q4
blocks.note: Each bar shows a factor's share of the five factors behind the risk score; factors with no noticeable effect are not shown. Red bars raise the risk and green bars lower it. These are the model's associations, not causes.

blocks.text: One validated news report about food conditions in Quezon was published in 2026 Q4.
The tone of the news and news reports that match none of the five factors account for about 6% of everything behind the score; news matched to a factor is counted within that factor.
The news for 2026 Q4 is not complete: the quarter is still running and reports are still being collected. The 2026 Q4 forecast was built from the news of 2026 Q3: no validated news reports.

items: The risk score is the estimated chance that the combined hunger-and-food-price score is above its usual level. It is not a measure of hunger or of how many families lack food.

By the study's rule (at least 75% correct on past quarters), results one quarter ahead are the reliable horizon: 78% were correct on development data. Results two quarters ahead were correct 67% of the time, so the two-quarter-ahead value shown here is an experimental preview.
City and municipal figures follow their province's score. They are not separate estimates for each city or municipality.
This is not an official food insecurity classification. The report presents findings only; it does not recommend actions and should be used alongside DA Region IV-A's own guidance.
